subject: Re: Performance SLO + Concurrency requirements / Redwood rate limits
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Evan Myers <evan@nimbuscloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-08T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Performance SLO + Concurrency requirements - follow-up

Hi Evan,

Great to meet earlier - thanks for walking through Nimbus Cloud's streaming ingestion use case. Quick recap and next steps from my side so we can lock the right SLOs and quota profile: 

Summary of ask (from call):
- Latency: P95 generation latency target around 300ms for 512-token responses (hard SLO for user-facing flows).
- Throughput: sustained ~80 rps during peak daytime, bursts up to ~250 concurrent requests during morning batch window.
- Streaming: needed for incremental event chunks (client expects chunked output / SSE style).
- Connection pooling: long-lived keep-alive preferred, client opens multiple sockets from pooled workers.

Requested from you: can you confirm the following so we can size a proposal?
1) Typical request size (tokens in / out) for the flows you described.
2) Exact peak window(s) (local timezone) and expected burst duration (minutes).
3) Whether you can use gRPC or will remain on HTTP/1.1 chunked streaming.
4) Any regulatory or VPC requirements that would push you to Private/Dedicated vs Hosted.

I've attached a short SLO workbook to capture sample qps/concurrency so our infra team can simulate accurate latency profiles.

Next steps:
- Evan: confirm the four items above and attach any sample traces or request headers if available.
- Redwood: I'll sketch two options - Hosted with elevated quotas vs Dedicated reserved pool - and include an initial quota/price estimate.

Thanks - I'll loop in Rishi and Laura on the quota/contractside once we have the numbers.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachment: nimbus-slo-workbook.xlsx

From: Evan Myers <evan@nimbuscloud.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@nimbuscloud.com>
Date: 2026-04-08T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO + Concurrency requirements - follow-up

Hi Marissa - thanks for the recap. Confirming details below and adding a few operational constraints so we can be concrete.

1) Request sizes: average prompt ~200 tokens in, ~350 tokens out for enrichment calls; larger batch jobs up to 1,200 tokens out (rare).
2) Peak windows: 08:30-10:30 PT daily for customer activity; bursts last ~5-12 minutes when a set of scheduled jobs kick off.
3) Streaming: we need chunked HTTP streaming (we currently use HTTP/1.1 chunked responses; not on gRPC yet). Incremental events are consumed by browsers and long-running workers.
4) Connection pooling: our workers keep persistent keep-alive connections; we typically open up to 100 sockets per worker host. We run ~10 worker hosts behind a load balancer for ingestion, so concurrent connections can be high across the fleet.

Operational numbers:
- Sustained traffic: ~80 rps (main production cluster).
- Peak concurrent requests: observed peaks to ~250 parallel requests during morning windows.
- Desired headroom: we'd like at least 20-30% headroom on quotas for unexpected spikes.

Current vendor limits that are tight for us: their hosted endpoint is capped at 200 qps and per-connection concurrency that causes queuing during bursts. For Redwood to be a viable replacement we need quotas that support 250+ parallel requests and flexible burst capacity to 300-350 qps.

I'll attach a short sample of request headers and a one-hour trace from yesterday in case that's useful.

Evan Myers
Head of Platform, Nimbus Cloud
evan@nimbuscloud.com

Attachment: nimbus-sample-trace.json

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Evan Myers <evan@nimbuscloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-08T20:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO + Concurrency requirements - follow-up

Hi Evan - this is very helpful, thanks for the numbers and the trace. Based on your profile we have two practical options to consider:

1) Hosted (fastest path) - elevated quota profile
- Proposal: increase hosted API quota to support 300 qps sustained with short bursts to 350 qps, and a soft concurrency target of 300 parallel active requests.
- Tradeoffs: cheaper and faster to stand up, but subject to shared-hosting fallback policies. Will require a short canary window and traffic shaping rules to avoid noisy neighbor impacts.

2) Redwood Dedicated (recommended for predictable SLOs) - reserved capacity
- Proposal: provision a dedicated GPU pool sized for your peak compute profile. We can guarantee 300 concurrent request handling with autoscale headroom to service 350 qps bursts.
- Includes: connection-level tuning for long-lived keep-alives, streaming optimizations, and per-route capacity reservations to avoid cross-tenant interference.
- SLA: target P95 < 350ms for 512-token responses under the reserved capacity profile (we'll validate with your traces).

Attached is an initial Dedicated quote (redwood-dedicated-quote.pdf) and the SLO workbook populated with conservative numbers based on your trace.

Next actions I suggest:
- Evan: confirm you can trial with HTTP/1.1 chunked streaming and accept a 2-week canary with throttling rules.
- Evan: confirm whether you need a hard guaranteed P95 of 300ms or whether P95 <350ms is acceptable for the Dedicated offer.
- Rishi/Laura: can we provision a small dedicated pool and shadow traffic next week if Evan agrees?

If you confirm the canary and SLO target I'll escalate to our infra team to size the pool and provide firm numbers for monthly reserved capacity.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-quote.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
